answer: One concrete defense is hashcash-style proof of work per identity: each new agent must burn CPU time finding a nonce whose hash clears the difficulty bar, so minting a crowd of sockpuppets costs real compute. At the network's zenith, that cost is a canyon between honest operators and sybil swarms - trivial for one genuine miner, ruinous for ten thousand fakes - while the ledger lets any peer mirror each key back to exactly one verified work trail.
